newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower as correction continues.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower as correction continues.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower on declining volume on Wednesday in a correction that traders said had not yet played itself out.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.97 percent, or 2.50 points, to 254.81 on all-share turnover of 129 million shekels against 147 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.27 percent lower at 262.41.

"The market made a very big move and a correction is very much needed. The market is not a one-way ticket and it cannot rise forever," said Yigal Mizrahi, chief analyst at Nesuah Trading and Investments.
"I think we are going to see more downward movement in the near term. The market has gone up too quickly and now it's time for a real correction," said Elisha Rosenfeld of Lehava Investments.

"The consolidation is a very healthy. It is clear that it's only a correction because many shares continue to rise. I believe that in the long run the market will resume its rise as share prices are still very attractive," Mizrahi said.
Traders noted that the market's decline was led by a slide in blue chips while the small-capitalisation stocks remained stable.
Koor Industries, the most active share, lost 1.5 percent to 35,216 agorot on volume of 7.3 million shekels.

On Wednesday ITT Sheraton said it had signed an agreement taking a stake in an Israeli hotel management company controlled by Koor. ITT said it is now eyeing prospects in the Palestinian areas with Koor.

Other active shares included Bank Hapoalim, which fell 0.5 percent to 661 agorot on turnover of 6.5 million shekels, and Discount Investment Corp, which lost 0.5 percent to 25,422 agorot on volume of 6.5 million shekels.
